walkthroughs.body_html:
Space Physics — a core area of GCSE Physics.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Space Physics brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Space Physics.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Redshift of distant galaxies is evidence that:
options: the universe is contracting
galaxies are heating up
the universe is expanding
light slows over distance

mcqs.q: The Sun is currently in which stage?
options: Protostar
Main sequence
Red giant
White dwarf

mcqs.q: What does a concave lens do to parallel rays of light?
options: It converges them to a focal point in front of the lens.
It diverges them — they spread out as if from a virtual focal point behind the lens.
The metal absorbs the heat from the air, leaving it colder than wood.
It reflects them back the way they came.

mcqs.q: Why does a metal surface feel colder than a wooden surface in the same room?
options: The metal absorbs the heat from the air, leaving it colder than wood.
The metal is actually colder than the wood.
Metal conducts heat away from your hand more quickly than wood, so it removes thermal energy faster — even though both are at room temperature.
Thick lead — only lead can stop any radiation.

mcqs.q: What absorber is needed to stop beta radiation?
options: A sheet of paper — beta is only slightly more penetrating than alpha.
A few millimetres of aluminium (or similar thin metal sheet).
Thick lead — only lead can stop any radiation.
The metal absorbs the heat from the air, leaving it colder than wood.
